clue.text: Waste vehicle finally had American expanse turned over

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word had
turned over means the word for expanse is flipped end to end

parts.note: a tract is a wide expanse of land

explanation.surface: Someone complains that an American finally flipped over a great stretch of land in a rubbish truck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned over' flips TRACT to give TCART.
explanation.definitionFit: A dustcart is the British name for a refuse lorry that collects household rubbish.

clue.text: Locations of strip shows? Time to strip

parts.note: dives are seedy bars and clubs, the sort of place for a strip show

explanation.surface: A question about where strip shows are held, then a call that it is time to undress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locations of strip shows' looks like a definition but gives DIVES.
explanation.definitionFit: To divest is to take off clothing or to deprive of something, so it means to strip.

clue.text: Leader of Strangeways team?

indicators.note: leader of signals the first letter of Strangeways

parts.note: a crew is a team working together

explanation.surface: Who heads the staff at Strangeways, a prison in Manchester?
explanation.walkthrough: Strangeways is a well-known prison in Manchester, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Screw is British slang for a prison warder, the sort who runs a team at a jail.

clue.text: E.g. C Chaplin cavorting? It's sweet stuff

indicators.note: cavorting means capering about, so these letters skip into a new order

explanation.surface: Charlie Chaplin larking about on screen is sweet to watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cavorting' rearranges EG and CCHAPLIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A cling peach is a variety of peach whose flesh clings to the stone, a sweet fruit.

clue.text: Youngster trimming new shirt

indicators.note: trimming means cutting off, so the new letter is removed

parts.note: a teen is a youngster

explanation.surface: A youngster altering a new shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: TEEN without N leaves TEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tee is short for T-shirt, a casual short-sleeved shirt.

clue.text: Fine arrangement for 9 Across, emotional

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: an arrangement of music reworks material, so the composer's name is rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 9 Across is the composer of the opera Falstaff

explanation.surface: A fine orchestral arrangement of a piece by an Italian composer stirs the emotions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' rearranges VERDI into ERVID.
explanation.definitionFit: Fervid describes intense, passionate feeling, close in sense to emotional.

clue.text: Test energy climbing peak

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: max is short for maximum, the peak

explanation.surface: A test of stamina climbing a mountain peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns MAX into XAM.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is a formal test of knowledge.

clue.text: Justify possibly rude sign on show

parts.note: the V-sign is an insulting hand gesture in Britain, so a rude sign may be V
to indicate is to show, point out

explanation.surface: Someone defends a vulgar gesture made in public.
explanation.walkthrough: The British V-sign, two fingers with the palm inward, is an obscene gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: To vindicate is to show to be right, to justify.

clue.text: Teetotaller's attitude regarding certain constructions?

parts.note: a dry is someone who does not drink, so a teetotaller's is dry's
tone means manner or attitude

explanation.surface: A nondrinker's disapproving manner towards certain buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: Drystone walls are built of stones without mortar, so the word describes such constructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Drystone describes walls laid without mortar, so it concerns a particular kind of construction.

clue.text: Falstaff's creator — something of a clever dick

indicators.note: something of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The creator of Falstaff is described as a bit of a smart alec.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Verdi composed the opera Falstaff, his final work for the stage.

clue.text: Inert clay needing animating for sure

indicators.note: the dead clay must be brought to life, so its letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A sculptor's lifeless clay definitely needs bringing to life.
explanation.definitionFit: Certainly and for sure are both adverbs of firm assurance, simple synonyms.

clue.text: Points of attraction I'd found in trophies and violin that's turned up

indicators.note: found in means the I'd letters go inside the trophies word

parts.note: cups are trophies
taken as written, without the apostrophe

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the violin word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: a Strad is a Stradivarius violin

explanation.surface: Things that attract notice include trophies and an old violin that has appeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses STRAD to DARTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupid's darts are the arrows of love, so their points draw lovers together.

clue.text: Extra custom from another lot of monks?

definitions.meaning: further business from a customer who buys the same again
a religious community is an order, so another such community is a second order

explanation.surface: Extra business arrives from a second group of monks.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeat order is a further purchase of the same goods; read literally it is a second monastic order.

clue.text: Bob plugging trickle that is limiting pressure in waste disposal unit

indicators.note: plugging means stopping a gap, so this piece goes inside the trickle word

parts.note: to seep is to trickle slowly through
to bob is to move up and down, like a dog's tail when it wags

indicators.note: limiting means bounding on both sides, so the that-is letters surround the pressure letter

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A bobbing object blocking a slow trickle under pressure in a drain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a name but means wag, as a tail does; 'plugging' and 'limiting' each signal one piece sitting inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A sewage pipe carries waste water away, so it is literally a unit for disposing of waste.

clue.text: Horse not getting over quantity of water?

indicators.note: not getting means the over letter is left out of the horse word

parts.note: a pinto is a piebald horse
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A horse refuses to jump the water obstacle.
explanation.walkthrough: PINTO without O leaves PINT.
explanation.definitionFit: A pint is a measure of liquid volume, so it can describe a quantity of water; the question mark marks the loose example.

clue.text: Most of team engaged in banal filming of everyday life

indicators.note: engaged in means the shortened team word sits inside the banal word

parts.note: trite means banal, hackneyed

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the team word is dropped

parts.note: an eleven is a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: Most of a team takes part in some dull documentary footage.
explanation.walkthrough: An eleven is a cricket or football side of eleven players; 'Most of' drops its final letter and 'engaged in' puts the rest inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Televerite is a documentary style showing real people's daily lives on television.

clue.text: This device police initially put in spot — car made to behave differently?

definitions.text: This device police initially put in spot — car made to behave differently?

indicators.note: put in means the police letter goes inside the spot word

parts.note: to spot is to see

indicators.note: initially signals the opening letter of police
behaving differently means the letters of car made change their order

explanation.surface: A roadside device the police install so that drivers change how they drive.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a speed camera is meant to make drivers slow down. 'put in' and 'to behave differently' are the two indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: A speed camera is a police roadside device that makes motorists slow down.

clue.text: Fight with hitmen — not one left — for gems

parts.note: to spar is to fight, box

indicators.note: not means the one and left letters are taken away

parts.note: hitmen are hired killers
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A brawl with contract killers in which nobody survives, all over jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: KILLERS without I and L leaves KLERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparklers is slang for diamonds or other gems.

clue.text: Clubs ahead in tournament

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
up means in the lead, as in two up

explanation.surface: A golf team with its clubs is leading in a competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup is a knockout tournament named after its trophy, like the FA Cup.

clue.text: Face chap upset about shed? An unknown quantity

indicators.note: about means the rearranged chap letters go round the shed and unknown pieces
upset means knocked over, so the letters of chap are rearranged

parts.note: a hut is a shed
Z is a letter used in algebra for an unknown

explanation.surface: Someone's nerve when a chap is upset about his shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns CHAP into CPAH; 'about' puts HUTZ inside it after the C.
explanation.definitionFit: Face in the sense of brazen nerve matches chutzpah, shameless audacity.

clue.text: International appearing in first half of test match

indicators.note: appearing in means the international letter sits inside the other piece
first half of takes the opening two of the four letters of test

explanation.surface: A capped player turns out in the first half of a test match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first half of' takes TE from test; 'appearing in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie is a sporting fixture between two sides, especially a cup match.

clue.text: Cleric's office ceased working with choir

indicators.note: working means operating, so these letters are set going in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A clergyman's office stopped functioning along with the choir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges CEASED and CHOIR together.
explanation.definitionFit: An archdiocese is the district under an archbishop, so it is the office or jurisdiction of a senior cleric.

clue.text: Not warm, cold, though short of Everest levels?

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
hilly country is raised but falls short of mountainous heights

explanation.surface: It is cold up there, though nowhere near as high as Everest.
explanation.walkthrough: C is cold, as on a tap.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilly means cool, not warm.

clue.text: Risk losing initial receipts

indicators.note: losing initial means the first letter of the risk word is dropped

parts.note: a stake is something put at risk, a wager

explanation.surface: A gambler takes a chance by losing early takings.
explanation.walkthrough: STAKE without its first letter S leaves TAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: The take is money received, such as box-office takings or receipts.

clue.text: Heard woman in white's annoyed comment about closing of current riding trail

indicators.note: heard means the bride word is said aloud, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: a woman in white is a bride, so her things are bridal

indicators.note: about means the pah letters wrap round the closing letter

parts.note: pah is an exclamation of irritation

indicators.note: closing of signals the last letter of current

explanation.surface: A bride grumbles about the end of a current as she rides along a trail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closing of' gives T from current; 'about' puts it inside PAH for PATH.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridle path is a track meant for horse riders, a riding trail.

clue.text: A recording leads to havoc around major star

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record

indicators.note: leads to signals the first letters of havoc and around

explanation.surface: A record causes chaos around a big celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads to' picks H and A from havoc around.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the brightest star in a constellation, so a major star.

clue.text: Game, flashy, but offering nothing at the end

indicators.note: the nothing letter is shifted to the end of the flashy word

parts.note: loud means garish, flashy

explanation.surface: A game that looks flashy but gives you nothing in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The O (nothing) in LOUD moves to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludo is a board game of dice and counters.

clue.text: Earlier figure repeats nothing in publicity work

indicators.note: in means the repeats-and-nothing letters go inside the publicity letters

parts.note: PR is public relations, publicity work
recurs means happens again, repeats
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A forerunner keeps coming to nothing in the PR business.
explanation.walkthrough: PR, public relations, is the standard crossword shorthand for publicity work; 'in' puts the other pieces inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A precursor is someone or something that comes before, a forerunner or earlier figure.

clue.text: Nobleman removing hat? That's uncalled-for

indicators.note: removing hat means taking off the top letter of the nobleman word

parts.note: a toff is a posh aristocratic person

explanation.surface: A nobleman doffing his hat is told the gesture is unnecessary.
explanation.walkthrough: TOFF without its first letter T leaves OFF.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark that is off is out of order, unacceptable or uncalled-for.

clue.text: Urge merely to get naked around Spain

indicators.note: around means the stripped word goes round the Spain letter
getting naked means stripping off the outer layer, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: simply means merely, just
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Someone is pushed simply to strip off on a Spanish beach.
explanation.walkthrough: SIMPLY without its first and last letters is IMPL; 'around' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or push someone to act, the same as to urge.

clue.text: Variable source of salve found in revolutionary fancy herb

indicators.note: found in means these letters sit inside the fancy word
revolutionary means turning round, so the fancy word is read backwards

parts.note: posh means fancy, smart
Y is a letter used in algebra as a variable

indicators.note: source of signals the first letter of salve

explanation.surface: A variable healing ingredient is found in a radical upmarket herb blend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns POSH into HSOP; 'source of' gives S; 'found in' puts YS inside HSOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyssop is an aromatic plant of the mint family used as a culinary and medicinal herb.

clue.text: Allied states supplied crude, securing energy

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the energy letter is gripped between the other pieces

parts.note: fed means supplied, provided with
racy means risque, crude
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Allies provided crude oil in return for securing energy supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'securing' has the two outer pieces holding the energy letter between them, rather than one word wrapping round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A federacy is a federation, a league of allied states joined together.
